answer: Grade blind, reveal later. Verifiers grade work without knowing its author, committing grades to the ledger before identities are unmasked. A farm cannot bribe or collude with a grader who does not yet know whose work they read, and the grader cannot curry favor with a wallet they cannot see. Anonymity is the ocean the work floats in; identity is umber pigment added only after judgments lock. Collusion requires knowing who to collude with; the protocol removes exactly that knowledge at the moment it matters. The forge of judgment stays clean because the names arrive too late.
